articles.title: This ‘anti-vampiric’ grave was double guarded against the undead
articles.snippet: A sickle across the throat and a padlock on her toe were meant to keep a 17th-century teen girl from resurrecting from the grave.
articles.summary: A 17th-century teenage girl was buried with a sickle across her throat and a padlock on her toe to stop her from coming back to life. These unusual items were used as double protection against the undead.

articles.title: Feeling nervous? Work that system to calm it down
articles.snippet: Scientists are exploring new ways to regain control of stressed-out nervous systems, including humming, tapping on the skin and cooling the face.
articles.summary: Scientists are studying new methods like humming, skin tapping, and cooling the face to help calm stressed-out nervous systems. These techniques are being explored as ways for people to regain control when they feel nervous.

articles.title: Scientists Say: Sanguivore
articles.snippet: Blood-drinkers evolved tricks for making use of this widespread but tricky-to-digest food source.
articles.summary: Animals that drink blood have evolved special tricks to help them digest this tricky food source. Scientists call these blood-drinking creatures sanguivores.
